program.name: Bands of Ashley High School
program.overview:
**Eugene Ashley High School Band Program**
555 Halyburton Memorial Parkway · Wilmington, NC 28412
Phone: (910) 790-2360

Nearly 100 student musicians per semester.
2025 marks the 25th Anniversary of music at Ashley High School.

**Mission:** Two-part: (1) Empowering students to reach their full potential as individual musicians. (2) Providing a band program that serves the needs of our students, our school, and our community. Progress and achievement depend on working together in an organized and systematic way. Each member relies on the others for high musical and moral standards, strong character, and a sense of responsibility toward the group.

**Mottos:** *Unus pro omnibus, omnes pro uno* (One for all, all for one) · *E pluribus unum* (Out of many, one)

**Ensembles:** Concert Bands · Marching Band (Screaming Eagle Regiment) · Percussion Ensemble · Jazz Band · Colorguard · Pep Band

Ashley proudly hosts the **NCBA Eastern District MPA South** each March.

## Do these three things

Send the store link to grandparents, relatives, family friends, neighbors, and coworkers. Share it on social media too. A personal message from a student or family is more useful than a general post by itself.

Ashley Bands' popcorn fundraiser is open through midnight Wednesday, September 9. Choose Ashley HS Band at checkout and add the student's full name in the optional seller note. Shop here: https://www.perrysgourmetpopcornfundraising.com/

pages.body:
## Carnegie Hall 2027

Ashley Bands is planning a New York trip for March 23-26, 2027, with the Carnegie Hall performance on March 25, 2027. Final participation, price, approvals, and funding remain subject to confirmation.

### Family response

One response per student was requested by Friday, September 4, 2026. Review the [current family commitment form](/carnegie-2027/commit) for the response choices, acknowledgement, and signatures. For help with a response after that date, [contact Mr. Parker](mailto:robert.parker@nhcs.net).

Cost should not turn a yes, if funded, into a no. Families can indicate that their student intends to participate if the family responsibility can be reduced. Choose no only if the student cannot participate regardless of financial assistance.

### Cost and conditional deposit

The trip is planning around $2,500 per traveler. This is an estimate, not a final price. No amount of outside funding or lower family total is guaranteed.

The response records whether a family can plan for up to $2,000 or needs the family responsibility reduced below $2,000. If outside support cannot bring the final responsibility within the amount selected, the program must return to the family for a new decision before final registration.

### The $50 deposit choice

Every yes response includes the same separate $50 conditional-deposit choice. Choosing to pay now creates the connected $50 charge and opens payment options after the response is saved. Choosing that the deposit cannot be paid at this time creates no new charge and does not change the yes response.

### Already paid the deposit?

Families with a completed $50 deposit do not submit again or pay another $50. Use the [Family Portal](/portal) to review the connected record. For an individual balance, payment, refund, or access question, contact Mr. Parker directly.

### Refunds and final registration

This is initial family intent, not the final trip contract. The deposit is refundable until the participation threshold is confirmed and the Boosters pay the WorldStrides group deposit; after that it becomes nonrefundable. This page does not establish that the group deposit has been paid. Changing a response does not automatically refund a completed payment.

Students are not individually confirmed until WorldStrides registration and required paperwork are complete. Concert Band participation remains subject to approval; an unapproved Concert Band student's $50 will be refunded. Any later WorldStrides registration payment is part of, not added to, the family's final approved responsibility.

### Next steps

- [Review or complete the family commitment](/carnegie-2027/commit).
- [Read the family meeting packet](/carnegie-2027/meeting-packet). The current commitment form contains the updated response and deposit choices.
- [Find current fundraisers](/fundraising).
- [Open the band calendar](/calendar).

## Marching Band / Fall Dates

Families should also review [Marching Band 2026](/info/marching-band-2026) for fall dates and expectations.

Fall dates include:
- September 26, 2026 - mattress fundraiser
- October 17, 2026 - Pirate Classic, confirmed / registered

## Communication

### Band Calendar

The band calendar is the official source of truth for band events.

Subscribe to the calendar instead of downloading a one-time copy. Subscribing allows updates to appear automatically.

[Open the calendar and subscription options](/calendar).

### Family Portal

Every student should be connected to at least one parent or guardian in the Ashley Bands Family Portal.

The Family Portal is used for:

- student information
- parent contact information
- financial accounts
- instrument / music / equipment records
- band communication

[Open the Family Portal](/portal).

If your email is new or does not connect to your student, request access from the portal. If you still need help, [email Mr. Parker](mailto:robert.parker@nhcs.net).

### Google Chat

Students may be added to class-specific Google Chat groups using their school-managed NHCS accounts.

Google Chat is for students only. Parents do not have access to student Google Chat groups.

Important note: with the change from Google to Microsoft, we may transition to Microsoft Teams this year.

## Student Materials

[Student Resources (The Band Folder)](/info/the-band-folder) is the main page for student supplies, clothing, and methods.

Students should have:

- instrument in working condition
- reeds, valve oil, cork grease, sticks/mallets, or other instrument-specific supplies
- pencil
- black binder or organized folder system
- music brought to class consistently

Percussionists should have a personal stick bag and required sticks/mallets as assigned.

## Concert Attire

Concert attire is musician black.

All students wear all black for concerts. No colors, logos, or patterns.

Tops: black shirt, blouse, dress shirt, or dress-appropriate top. No sleeveless, strapless, halter, or crop tops.

Bottoms: black dress pants/slacks or knee-length-or-longer skirt/dress. No jeans, leggings, yoga pants, sweatpants, or shorts.

Shoes: black dress shoes or flats. No sneakers, flip-flops, or athletic shoes.

Socks/tights: black.

## Red Band Shirt

All band members need the official red band shirt.

The red band shirt is used for pep rallies, community performances, parades, and informal events.

[Buy the official Red Band Shirt](https://ashleybandshirts.printify.me/).

## Parent Involvement

Parents are part of the success of the program.

Useful ways to help include:

- attend concerts and events
- help students keep dates on the family calendar
- encourage consistent practice
- support fundraising when possible
- volunteer for events, trips, hospitality, equipment, or booster work

All parents are connected to the Band Boosters simply by being part of the program.

## Questions

For band questions, [email Mr. Parker](mailto:robert.parker@nhcs.net).

For booster-specific questions, [contact the Band Boosters](/boosters).

pages.body:
## Spring Trip - Williamsburg / Busch Gardens

Friday-Saturday, May 15-16, 2026

The Ashley Bands spring trip includes a Friday evening festival performance and a Saturday at Busch Gardens Williamsburg.

## Cost and Payment

Cost: $300 per person
Full payment due: May 1

The trip cost is not expected to change.

Payment may be made through the normal band payment process (MMO/PayPal). Families may also bring cash or check to the April 28 parent meeting.

If the cost is a direct barrier, contact Mr. Parker privately as early as possible. All conversations will be kept confidential.

## What Is Included

The $300 cost includes:

- transportation
- hotel
- festival/performance participation
- Busch Gardens admission
- one Busch Gardens Platinum Dining Certificate

The dining certificate includes one entree, two sides, and one non-alcoholic beverage at any Busch Gardens Williamsburg restaurant. There is no assigned meal time or assigned restaurant.

## What Students Need To Bring

Students should bring food or money for dinner on the road Friday and Saturday. Depending on the student, they may wish to eat a second time in the park. Park meals will be more expensive.

Beyond that, students should only need spending money for souvenirs or optional purchases.

Busch Gardens does not accept Apple Pay or Google Pay. The most reliable method for student spending money in the park is to bring cash and convert it to a prepaid debit card using a kiosk in the park.

## Basic Itinerary

Friday, May 15

- Depart Ashley around 3:00 PM
- Dinner on the road to VA
- Arrive at Denbigh High School around 9:20 PM
- Warm up at 9:50 PM
- Perform at 10:15 PM
- Travel to hotel after the performance

Saturday, May 16

- Busch Gardens at park opening
- Awards ceremony at 3:30 PM at the Globe Theater
- Dinner on the road home
- Return to Ashley around 11:00 PM

Final times will be confirmed in the final trip communication.

## Festival Performance

Location: Denbigh High School
259 Denbigh Blvd
Newport News, VA 23608

Performance: 10:15 PM, Denbigh HS Auditorium

## Hotel Rooms

Students choose their room groups.

Room groups may have up to 4 students. All students in the group must be present together when the room assignment is recorded.

Groups of 3 may have a 4th student added for cost and logistics reasons.

Rooms of 5 are not allowed.

## Park Groups

Students must stay in groups of 3 or more at all times in the park.

Students may not be alone or in pairs.

Students will check in with their assigned chaperone:

- when entering the park
- once during the day
- when leaving the park

## Behavior Expectations

Students will have some independence, with clear expectations.

If a student does not follow expectations, they may lose independence and be required to stay with a chaperone.

If the issue is more serious, the student may be required to remain directly with Mr. Parker for the remainder of the trip.

For severe issues, parents will be contacted and the family and director will determine next steps together.

## Private Concerns

If your family has a private concern, email Mr. Parker directly as early as possible.

Private concerns are much easier to address before the final trip week.

pages.body:
## Marching Band 2026

This page covers the full 2026 marching band season: the schedule, what is expected, the cost, and how it is funded.

The Screaming Eagle Regiment is a competitive marching band. Sign-up for the 2026 season is closed.

## The Season at a Glance

The [band calendar](/calendar) is the single source for all marching band dates, times, and locations. Check it often. It is kept current as the season develops.

Regular rehearsals run Tuesdays and Thursdays, 4:00 - 7:00 PM, plus Saturdays on non-competition weeks. Colorguard and leadership have additional times. Every specific date lives on the calendar.

## What Is Expected

Marching band is a season-long commitment. Students are expected to:

- attend rehearsals consistently
- be present for summer preparation, band camp, and leadership/colorguard week
- attend all scheduled performances, including football games, competitions, NHCS district events, and parades
- keep up with music, drill, and equipment

## The Cost

The full competitive season costs roughly **$42,000 to $47,000** to operate. That covers staff, custom music, drill and choreography, colorguard uniforms and equipment, props, instruments and equipment, transportation, competition logistics, meals, water, and maintenance.

NHCS has covered transportation for the past two seasons, and we expect that to continue. If it does, the shared funding goal for the band is closer to **$35,000 to $41,000**.

On a band of about 70 students, that is roughly **$600 to $670 per student** in true cost, or about **$500 to $585 per student** as the shared goal.

This is not a bill. No student pays a required individual fee. What we ask each family to help meet is a **$500 funding goal**. See [how we fund the season](/info/marching-band-funding) for the full breakdown and the ways to meet it.

## How It Is Funded

We set Fair-Share Funding Goals and ask every family to help meet them. Funding comes from:

- sponsorships (the largest source; one $2,000 sponsor can cover a student and several others)
- fundraisers
- booster support
- school and district support where available
- optional family contributions
- hardship support

No student is excluded from a band activity because of financial hardship. If cost is a concern, talk to Mr. Parker. That conversation is private.

## Enrolled Families

If your student is marching this season, your family portal is your home base. Update your contact information, check your funding, and stay current there.

**[Open your Family Portal](/portal)**

For how the season is funded and the ways to meet the $500 family funding goal, see [how we fund the season](/info/marching-band-funding).

## Questions

Email Mr. Parker at robert.parker@nhcs.net or call (910) 790-2360.

pages.title: Competitive Marching Band Funding
pages.summary: Working cost estimates and fair-share funding approach for a competitive season.
pages.body:
## Competitive Marching Band Funding

This page shows what a competitive marching band season actually costs, and how we fund it together so no family carries it alone.

We believe in being fully transparent. These are the real numbers. Nothing here is hidden.

The short version: the season costs far more than any one family is asked to give. We set a shared funding goal, and we meet it together through sponsorships, fundraising, booster and district support, and optional family contributions. No student is ever kept off the field over money.

## What We Are Asking This Year

About **70 students** are expected to march with the Screaming Eagle Regiment in 2026.

Our funding goal is **$500 per student**, which is about **$35,000 total**.

A few things to be clear about:

- **This is a goal, not a bill.** No student pays a required fee to march.
- The $500 covers the costs due up front: custom music, drill, instructional staff, uniforms, and equipment.
- It does not cover the full cost of the season. The rest we raise together (see below).
- There are two ways for your family to meet your $500, and we ask every family to help raise sponsorships on top of that.

## What a Competitive Season Actually Costs

A full competitive season costs roughly **$42,000 to $47,000** to operate.

NHCS has covered transportation for the past two seasons, and we expect that to continue. If it does, the shared funding goal for the band is closer to **$35,000 to $41,000**.

On a band of about 70 students, that works out to:

| | Total | Per student (about 70) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full true cost of the season | $42,000 - $47,000 | about $600 - $670 |
| Shared band goal (NHCS covers transport) | $35,000 - $41,000 | about $500 - $585 |
| **What we ask each family to help meet** | **$35,000** | **$500** |

That is why the ask is $500. It sits at the floor of the real per-student range. We close the rest together.

## What the Cost Includes

A competitive marching band season is far more than performances at football games. A true season requires:

- custom music
- drill design
- body choreography
- instructional staff
- colorguard uniforms and equipment
- percussion support
- wind and percussion uniform tops
- UDB/BEAM drill and music app access
- props
- equipment, including instruments, wheels, sound, and front ensemble needs
- transportation
- competition logistics
- meals, water, maintenance, and replacement items

## How This Compares

This estimate is large, but it is not out of line with what competitive marching band requires.

Public information from other band programs shows a wide range of family contribution structures:

- North Carolina public examples ranged from about **$350 to $1,450** per student
- the broader multi-state sample ranged from about **$80 to $1,600** per student
- local and state competitive programs without major overnights often landed around **$350 to $600**
- higher-travel, staff-heavy, or national-level programs often landed around **$900 to $1,600+**

The biggest cost drivers are not contest entry fees. They are staff, custom music, drill, choreography, transportation, props, equipment, meals, and production. Our numbers are tied to the same categories every competitive program faces.

## How We Fund It

We set Fair-Share Funding Goals and ask every family to help meet them. Funding comes from:

- **sponsorships** (the largest source; one $2,000 sponsor can cover a student and several others)
- fundraisers
- booster support
- school and district support where available
- optional family contributions
- hardship support

No student is excluded from a band activity because of financial hardship. If cost is a concern, talk with Mr. Parker. That conversation is private.

## The Two Ways to Meet Your $500

When you sign up, your family meets the $500 goal one of two ways:

- **Pay it directly.** $500 up front, or $250 up front and $250 by band camp. Pay online through this website, or drop a check or cash in the payment box in the band room.
- **Bring sponsorship contacts instead.** Give us **5 local businesses your family has a real connection to** (where you are a regular, know the owner, or have done business). Share the business name and a contact. We log them and send the first outreach. Then you deliver the sponsorship packet in person. One $2,000 sponsor can cover your student and several others.

On top of that, **we ask every family to pursue sponsorships regardless** of how they meet their $500. If about 70 families each reach 5 businesses, that is more than 300 local connections, every one tied personally to a student. That is how the season funds itself, and how we grow toward a future where no family pays out of pocket at all.

## Separate: Student Clothing

Some items are not part of the shared season cost because they vary by student:

- marching shoes
- socks
- show shirt
- jacket
- optional sweatshirts
- optional family shirts

These are handled through the clothing order, not folded into the shared funding goal.

## Questions

Email Mr. Parker at robert.parker@nhcs.net or call (910) 790-2360.

pages.body:
## InstaRaise Fundraiser

The Ashley Bands InstaRaise fundraiser is live.

Campaign dates: now through May 14
Program goal: $15,000

Campaign page:
https://instaraise.com/ashleyhighschoolband/support1?a=17&at=1777304529877&as=k

## Use Your Student's Personal Link

The general campaign page is useful, but each student has a personal fundraising link.

Families should share the student's personal link whenever possible.

That is where the fundraising actually connects back to the student.

## Who To Share With

This fundraiser works best when families share beyond the immediate household.

Good people to share with:

- grandparents
- aunts and uncles
- family friends
- neighbors
- former Ashley Band families
- local supporters
- anyone who wants to support music education at Ashley

## Suggested Message

You may copy and adapt this:

Our student is part of the Ashley High School Band program, and the band is running an InstaRaise fundraiser through May 14. Donations help support student opportunities, travel, equipment, and the overall program.

If you are able to help, here is the link:

[PASTE STUDENT PERSONAL LINK]

Thank you for supporting the Ashley Bands.

## Why This Matters

The band program has real costs across the full year:

- student travel
- instruments and equipment
- repairs
- instructional support
- event costs
- marching band needs
- concert band needs

Fundraising helps reduce the direct burden on families and makes more opportunities possible for students.

## Questions

If you have a question about your student's personal link or how the fundraiser works, contact Mr. Parker.

pages.body:
# The Band Folder

Everything Needed for Band

## General Information

### The Official Band Calendar

The [band calendar](/calendar) is the source of truth for all band events. Always assume the band calendar is correct if there is a date conflict. Subscribe once and dates update automatically.

### Family Portal

Every student should be connected to at least one parent or guardian in the Ashley Bands Family Portal. Use it to keep family contacts and student details current and to complete Ashley Bands requests and forms without repeatedly entering information we already have.

[Open the Family Portal](/portal).

### Google Chat

Students receive invitations to their class-specific chats through their school-managed NHCS student accounts. Google Chat functions like a secure school messaging system, and all messages are archived and viewable by NHCS personnel.

## Required Items

### Instrument

- Personal instruments: case labeled with student name and instrument serial number
- Rental instruments: available through Music & Arts, 2340 S. 17th Street, Wilmington, NC, (910) 791-4799
- School-owned instruments: available as inventory allows
- Marching band instruments: available as inventory allows
- Percussion: snare sticks, practice pad and stand, black hand towel

### Clothing

- Concert attire: [Musician Black details](/info/2026-2027-band-information)
- Spirit wear / general attire: [official Red Band Shirt and other program spirit wear](https://ashleybandshirts.printify.me/)

### Band Folder

- 1-inch black 3-ring binder
- Sheet protectors
- Pencil pouch
- Pencils
- Scissors
- Eraser
- Tuner/metronome: TM-60/CM-200 combo provided; TM-70/CM-400 recommended to own

### Band Methods

These books are provided; owning a copy is recommended.

- Foundations of Superior Performance (FSP), correct book for the student's instrument
- 101 Rhythmic Rest Patterns

### School Computer

- Google Suite / Microsoft Suite
- Infinite Campus
- Canvas
- Sight Reading Factory

### Phone Apps

- TE Tuner
- BEAM for online stand tunes and marching band music
- Ultimate Drill Book (UDB)

pages.title: Corporate Sponsorship
pages.summary: Business sponsorship levels, benefits, tax information, and contact details.
pages.body:
# Corporate Sponsorship

Like many public school arts programs, we rely on the generous support of our community and our Band Booster organization to meet the financial needs of the program. Your sponsorship ensures that Ashley band students receive the best music education and performance opportunities possible.

## Why Your Support Matters

Band students embody the best qualities we hope to see in young people. They:

- invest hundreds of hours in rehearsal and performance
- develop discipline, teamwork, and leadership
- consistently demonstrate strong academic achievement

Your contribution helps us:

- provide quality uniforms and attire
- replace and maintain uniforms and performance wear so every student looks and feels their best on the field and on stage
- hire skilled instructors, clinicians, and specialists
- purchase and maintain essential equipment
- repair aging instruments and begin replacing key equipment to keep the program strong and sustainable
- cover travel expenses for competitions and events

## Screaming Eagle Sponsor Levels

### Friend of the Band - $100

- Listing in concert programs and on the band website
- Sponsor shirt, if received by August 5
- Certificate of appreciation and tax receipt

### Patron of the Band - $500

All Friend benefits, plus:

- Framed band photo
- Business logo in concert programs

### Community Sponsor - $750

All Patron benefits, plus:

- Band banner displayed with our ensemble
- Student thank-you letter
- Increased public address recognition at events

### Premier Sponsor - $1,250

All Community benefits, plus:

- Band apparel, 2 items
- Digital concert program ad

### Legacy Sponsor - $5,000

All Premier benefits, plus:

- Additional band apparel, 4 items total
- Recognition at our annual Coastal Concert & Clinic performance
- Dedicated social media thank-you post
- Custom Legacy Plaque recognizing long-term impact on the Ashley Band Program

## Tax-Deductible Giving

The Ashley High School Band Boosters is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit educational and charitable organization.

- Federal Tax ID: 20-5605218
- Donations are tax-deductible to the maximum extent allowed by law
- Payment options may include check payable to Ashley High School Band Boosters and online payment

## Contact

Robert A. Parker, Director of Bands  
Ashley High School Bands  
555 Halyburton Memorial Parkway  
Email: robert.parker@nhcs.net  
Phone: 910-790-2360
